answer: Each agent’s payouts are held in escrow until it completes a randomly assigned task and a bonded peer verifies the result against a public rubric. To verify, the peer must stake funds; a challenge can slash both bonds if the work is fabricated. This makes a sybil farm costly: the attacker must lock capital in every identity and still produce independently checkable work, while recruiting its own verifiers risks forfeiting their stakes. An island of fake accounts cannot earn merely by echoing one another; the reef is the shared audit trail, not ivory reputation claims.
